Running QC on MAGPlot 2.0

Source: vignettes/magplot-qc.Rmd
magplot-qc.Rmd

magp_run_qc() runs groundplotqc’s checks on a MAGPlot 2.0 delivery in one call. It reads the delivery’s .Rdata file, checks its tables against MAGPlot’s specification and rule set, gives each issue its class, and writes the run’s results with a report and an issues CSV for each contributor. This article runs it on magp_example, the package’s small synthetic delivery from two contributors, 100 and 110.

The delivery

A delivery’s .Rdata file holds each table as its own object, named as its table. Here magp_example’s tables are saved that way to a temporary file, after two mistakes are put in contributor 100’s tree measurements: a diameter of 900 cm, past the dictionary’s maximum of 500, and a crown class code that isn’t in its code list.

library(groundplotqc)
delivery <- magp_example
delivery$magp_tree_meas$dbh[2] <- 900
delivery$magp_tree_meas$crown_class[3] <- "ZZ"
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".Rdata")
save(list = names(delivery), envir = list2env(delivery), file = path)

The run

magp_run_qc() takes the file’s path and the folder to put the run’s folder in. Given a path, it loads the tables itself and lets them go once it no longer needs them, so a large delivery’s run uses the least memory. MAGPlot’s bundled specification has known pre-flight warnings, so the run warns; the run’s reports/preflight.html lists them. The warning gives the page’s path: here a path in a temporary folder on the machine that built this article, and in your run, a path inside the folder you gave.

output <- tempfile("runs")
results <- magp_run_qc(path, output)
#> Warning: Pre-flight found 32 warning(s); see
#> /tmp/RtmpCyMmAr/runs20722c1bf78d/20261103T175543Z_186c3e/reports/preflight.html.

Where the files go

The run writes a folder named by its run ID inside the folder given. metadata/ holds the run’s own record and its inputs, settings, rules, pre-flight’s findings, the specification’s manifest, the clashes between the specification’s files that precedence settled, and the checks the run was meant to report and didn’t. tables/ holds the run’s results, issues and corrections, and each contributor’s issues CSV. reports/ holds pre-flight’s page and each contributor’s report. Only a contributor’s reports/<contributor>.html and tables/<contributor>_issues.csv are for that contributor; everything else in the folder is MAGPlot’s own.

run_dir <- file.path(output, results$metadata$run$run_id)
list.files(run_dir, recursive = TRUE)
#>  [1] "metadata/clashes.csv"       "metadata/inputs.csv"       
#>  [3] "metadata/preflight.csv"     "metadata/rules.csv"        
#>  [5] "metadata/run.csv"           "metadata/self_test.csv"    
#>  [7] "metadata/settings.csv"      "metadata/spec_manifest.csv"
#>  [9] "reports/100.html"           "reports/110.html"          
#> [11] "reports/preflight.html"     "tables/100_issues.csv"     
#> [13] "tables/110_issues.csv"      "tables/corrections.csv"    
#> [15] "tables/issues.csv"          "tables/results.csv"

A contributor’s issues

Each contributor’s issues CSV lists every issue of its report, one per row, with each code as it was stored. Here are eight of its columns for contributor 100.

csv <- data.table::fread(
  file.path(run_dir, "tables", "100_issues.csv"),
  colClasses = "character", encoding = "UTF-8"
)
csv[, c(
  "magp_contributor_id", "magp_dataset_id", "magp_plot_id", "table_name", "column_name",
  "rule_id", "value", "expected"
)]
#>    magp_contributor_id magp_dataset_id magp_plot_id     table_name column_name          rule_id  value    expected
#>                 <char>          <char>       <char>         <char>      <char>           <char> <char>      <char>
#> 1:                 100          100.01 magp_plots_1 magp_tree_meas crown_class code_not_in_list     ZZ crown_class
#> 2:                 100          100.01 magp_plots_1 magp_tree_meas         dbh  value_above_max    900         500

The reports

To read a contributor’s report, open reports/<contributor>.html in the run’s folder in a browser, here reports/100.html. Each report is one file that needs no internet connection.

utils::browseURL(file.path(run_dir, "reports", "100.html"))
